pinned_doh_absolute_deadline_fix.implementation: doh_query now shares one monotonic absolute deadline across pinned resolvers, reads the bounded response in read1 chunks, and refreshes the remaining socket timeout before each chunk. Slow-drip responses cannot extend the DoH query indefinitely. It also prevents an outer SIGALRM TimeoutError (an OSError subclass) from being swallowed by doh_query's resolver-fallback handler and followed by another unbounded resolver attempt: after the caught exception the monotonic deadline is checked before the next resolver.
pinned_doh_absolute_deadline_fix.test: Regression test advances a fake monotonic clock during chunked reads and verifies that the deadline expires before a second resolver attempt.
pinned_doh_absolute_deadline_fix.interpretation: This closes a discovered unbounded slow-drip DoH read path. It is not evidence that this defect caused Run #20's timeout overrun. Source-level review also found that the previous broad OSError fallback could catch the outer SIGALRM TimeoutError and continue to the next resolver. The new absolute deadline closes that specific timeout-propagation hole. The independent 7-minute process-guard / 9-minute step / 12-minute job overrun in Run #20 remains unexplained.
pinned_doh_absolute_deadline_fix.outer_sigalrm_regression_test: passed; simulates TimeoutError during read1, advances monotonic time beyond deadline, and verifies that doh_query does not try the next resolver.
pinned_doh_absolute_deadline_fix.run20_relevance: fetch_vpnobratto_bytes calls doh_query with a maximum four-second resolver timeout. Before this fix, doh_query used one inactivity-timeout response.read and caught the outer 20-second SIGALRM TimeoutError through its OSError fallback, potentially proceeding to another resolver without an absolute deadline. This is a plausible explanation for a profile fetch stalling at the last visible marker, but not proven because Run #20 terminal logs are unavailable; it does not explain the separate 7-minute GNU timeout and GitHub step/job timeout overrun.
